water and steam blancheing of rambutan significantly reduced browning enzymes activities but did not affect the antioxidant activities of the peel extracts.
both blanching methods were able to reduce the browning enzymes of rambutan peels and the antioxidant activities of the peels were not affected.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of blanching treatment on enzyme and antioxidant activity of rambutan.
the effect of blanching time on the enzyme activities, antioxidant activity, total phenolic contents and peel colour of rambutan.
the effect of water blanching on the browning enzyme activity of rambutan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blanching process is a good method to reduce the enzymatic activities of rambutans, which is a good way of extending the storage period of the fruits.
blanching of rambutan peels with either water or steam did not reduce the antioxidant activity of the peels.
blanching did not significantly affect the antioxidant activity of rambutan peels, but it did affect the enzyme activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water and steam blanches at 100 °C for 5 and 10 min, respectively, are the most suitable pretreatment for rambutan peel.
the blanching of rambutan skin by either water or steam for 2.5 min could be a good method to prevent enzymatic browning without reducing antioxidant activity of the final products.
water or steam blanching of rambutan peels for 5 and 10 min, respectively, could effectively reduce POD and PPO activity without affecting the antioxidant capacity of rambutan extract.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water and steam blanches can be applied to reduce the enzymatic browning of rambutan peels without significantly altering the antioxidant activity.

water blanching for 5 min or steam blanching for up to 15 min is sufficient to inactivate browning enzymes in rambutan peel, without significantly affecting the phenolic compounds and the antioxidant activity.
water blanching for 5 min or steam blanching for at least 10 min is sufficient to reduce the POD and PPO enzyme activities.
